epic.title: Phase 3 — Evaluation
epic.description: Adds evaluation on top of Phases 1–2: score configs and scores everywhere (API, SDK, UI, public-key feedback), score filters and analytics, annotation queues with atomic locking, LLM-as-a-judge templates/rules/worker jobs with a daily cost cap, versioned datasets, SDK and UI experiments, and a run comparison page. Delayed jobs are added to the queue port. Lite mode stays the test default and the suite stays offline.

stories.title: Foundation, score configs, scores and public feedback
stories.description: Settings, permissions, queue delay support and models for scores/queues. Score configs with validation, the public scores API, SDK score params, score filters/sorts in both stores, the pk-only feedback endpoint, settings tabs, and score chips/inputs/columns in the UI.
acceptance: An Admin creates NUMERIC/CATEGORICAL/BOOLEAN configs; out-of-range scores via API return 400; the data type is immutable once scores exist; archived configs are hidden from pickers but keep their scores (AC-9)
Filtering `quality >= 0.5` and sorting by `score:quality` desc (unscored last) work in the lite store and survive a reload via URL (AC-10)
A pk-only POST /api/public/feedback creates a score with CORS for allowed origins only, rejects non-public configs and is rate limited; pk-only auth is rejected everywhere else (AC-8)
Score chips, a Scores column and config-driven inputs show on traces, observations and sessions

tasks.title: Judge runner (eval_job handler)
tasks.description: evals/runner.py: the eval_job handler. It re-checks the filter (skipped if no longer matching), resolves variables, compiles the template, calls the Phase 2 provider layer with the schema as structured output (JSON-mode fallback plus tolerant parse), validates the output, writes one EVAL score (comment = reasoning, execution_id) and a judge trace in traceloom-eval (eval:<template>, cost from the Phase 1 engine) via accept_batch. Retries with backoff and jitter up to eval_max_attempts; capped, skipped and failed states; secret-scrubbed errors; idempotent score ids; manual retry. Registers the handler.
acceptance: Invalid JSON then valid output succeeds on attempt 2
Always-failing output ends `failed` after 3 attempts with a scrubbed error
The second call over a $0.01 cap is `capped` with the reason 'daily cost cap of $X reached' and is not retried that day
A missing variable, an archived config or a missing connection fails without retries
Re-delivery overwrites the same score
Tests use the FakeProvider only

Hook ingest/process.py after commit inside try/except. Add sweeper.set_due_jobs for due or stuck eval_executions and dataset_run_items.
acceptance: Of 20 `chat` traces only the hash-selected ones get an execution, and `other` gets none
Re-ingesting does not create a second execution
